title: Jacques Villery collecting songs at the old folks' home
summary: She recounts giving songs to young Jacques Villery at the home and discusses his family in the French Quarter.

venues.name: Home for the Aged (Sive des Vieillards)

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: It's not so long that I gave a young man, Villery. He had a box somewhat like that. And I was at the home. A la Sive des Vieillards, you know, old folks home.
Oh, yes.
And I gave him plenty of songs. Of course, I was younger than I am now. I could remember.
I wonder who that was.
His name was Jacques Villery.
Jacques Villery.
Mm-hmm. And he came one day at the home. And the mother superior says, call me and call two or three old Creoles in there. And we all gave songs. And now I just can't remember nothing.
What happened to him? Is he from here, Jacques?

He this young man? Yes. Oh, yes. His mother was a Miss Lanus. And his father was a Mr. Villery. Creole. Creole, born from here. And he was a very young man. But he went on with, these things were just beginning to come out, I believe.
Mm-hmm.
Yes, his name was Jacques Villery.
Well, I think he may still be around in town. That name is somehow familiar. Oh, is it familiar? The Villery's live in the French Quarter, some of them.
Mm-hmm.
The Villery's live where you used to live, nearby, huh?
Oh, yes. Oh.
Where do they live? They live on, uh...
Oh, it's a rampart. There was one Villery, rampart, and Esplanade.
Well, that's a drug store.
The druggist, yes. Are they relatives? Well, that was his nephew.
Oh, we can locate him then, huh? Yeah, that'll be interesting if he still had a...
That was his nephew, his brother's son. His name was Jacques. Mm-hmm.
